items_missed: No agenda statement setting time expectations ('I'll gather some details, then walk you through pricing, takes about 10-15 minutes') before jumping into date/inventory questions
No explicit 'sound good?' confirmation tied to the agenda
Origin/destination address and zip code never confirmed on the call
No question about narrow hallways, tight turns, or long carry distances
Packing needs never directly asked (customer volunteered she's self-packing, but the question itself was skipped)
No question about storage stops or additional stops
Access concerns (parking, complex layout) were inferred from Google Street View images rather than confirmed with the customer directly
No 'pricing is super simple' framing opener before launching into the rate breakdown
No Worries Damage Coverage (up to $2,000) never specifically named -- only a generic 'insurance that we placed on your move' mention
Meet Your Mover (photo/info email before move day) never mentioned
Clock explanation never stated that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, and no distinct 'does that make sense?' sense-check after covering the minimum/proration
Save Your Ass prep speech skipped entirely -- no consolidation tips, no 'take a carload' tip -- despite an easy opening with a small, mostly self-packed load
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' close
Hours / how to reach the branch never given
Customer's name ('Annette') used only once, in the opening greeting, and never again through the rest of the call
top_strength: Erik smoothly resolved a date conflict by offering the discounted Sunday slot and getting a quick yes, then ran an efficient room-by-room inventory (including garage and patio items) that produced a clear, accurate small-move estimate ($505-$606) and booked the job in under 9 minutes.
coaching_note: Layer in the three differentiator pitches (No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) and the Save Your Ass prep speech during the pricing walkthrough -- none of the four were mentioned on this call, and with a customer who is self-packing and moving mostly furniture, a 30-second consolidation/carload tip would have cost nothing and reinforced value before the booking ask.
phone_presence_notes: Erik stayed upbeat and polite throughout, but leaned on repeated scripted affirmations ('perfect,' 'awesome,' 'sweet') rather than varied, natural warmth, and used the customer's name only once after the opening greeting.
